descriptionChirho: The noun rav (II) as a title meaning 'chief, captain, head official,' used in compound titles for Babylonian and Assyrian court officers (rav-tabbach 'chief of the guard,' rav-saris 'chief eunuch,' etc.). All four clusters denote the same official title: singular construct chief-of (25x), plural chiefs-of (1x), conjoined plural and-the-chiefs-of (1x), and steward-of (1x, still denoting the chief/head of a household). Arabic ra'isu/rabbu (رَئِيسُ/رَبُّ) 'chief/lord,' Spanish jefe-de 'chief of,' Hindi pradhan (प्रधान) 'chief,' Korean jang (장) 'head/chief,' and Swahili mkuu-wa 'chief of' converge across all clusters.
